title: A few named procedures, the same steps
statement: Teach a small fixed set of named thinking procedures that covers every skill the course models, with identical steps each time, and say the procedure's name whenever it is modelled.
example: Seven procedures cover every skill one grade 3 reading course models, so its students learn seven ways of thinking rather than dozens of isolated skills.
detail: A grade 3 reading course built its modelling around seven procedures that together cover every skill component it models (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/pedagogy/modelling-moment-procedures.md`, line 22). A later rule has each lesson name the procedure it teaches, such as finding or inferring, and teach the identical steps every time that procedure appears. The course's modelling rule adds that the name is itself the tool: a child who watched one procedure four times without once hearing its name was given four demonstrations and no tool. The contract checks that a named procedure is one of the seven, though whether a lesson names one at all is still left to convention (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/rules/pedagogy-and-lesson-structure.md`, lines 351-355).

evidence.quote: Seven procedures cover every Standard Component used in this curriculum as a Modelling Moment target. Students learn seven ways of thinking, not dozens of isolated skills.
A lesson names the comprehension procedure it teaches, for example FIND or INFER, and the child is taught the identical sequential steps every time that procedure appears.
Seven named procedures are the whole design: a child who has watched FIND four times without once hearing it called FIND has been given four demonstrations and no tool.
